policies.name: Rationing
policies.description: We will ration food and consumer goods, and every household will receive its share by coupon.
policies.note: The consumer share it takes is what the population feels, through the consumer goods shortage curve under Resources. A flat happiness figure on top would charge the same goods twice.

policies.name: Lobby for a law
policies.description: Our ministers, editors and party members will campaign for a new law.
policies.note: Lobbying persuades people who can be voted out, so it needs a government that can be. Elections are read from the form of government, or from the polity's own entry where it departs from the form. The target is a law as {law, option}, both named because an option name alone is ambiguous, or a decree as {decree}. Only decrees marked lobbyable may be named: property, land, the church and labour law are what a chamber fights over, and martial law is a thing a government does. The target decides which of the two costs is charged. Where the decree names a target of its own the discount covers it whichever one is chosen, since what is being lobbied for is nationalisation and not one particular pit.

policies.name: War bonds
policies.description: We will sell war bonds to our people to fund our war effort.

policies.name: Officer training
policies.description: Our staff colleges will train more officers than our army needs.

policies.name: Civil defence
policies.description: We will build air-raid shelters, train wardens and move our industry out of the cities.

policies.name: Improve worker conditions
policies.description: We will limit working hours and set wages and safety standards in our factories by law.

policies.name: Foreign investment
policies.description: We will invest state money in another country's industry.

policies.name: Consolidate the colonies
policies.description: We will send administrators, garrisons and teachers out to our colonies.
policies.note: The answer to an empire slipping away, and it is paid for out of the empire. A country stops taking three tenths of what its colonies remit, on top of the upkeep, so holding them by administration costs about what holding them by extraction earned. A country with no colonies cannot start it.

policies.name: Public works
policies.description: We will put the unemployed to work building roads, canals and public buildings.

policies.name: Propaganda
policies.description: Our information office will supply the press and cinemas with official material.

policies.name: Industrial subsidies
policies.description: We will pay our manufacturers a fixed sum for every unit they produce.

policies.name: Armaments drive
policies.description: We will pay for extra shifts in our arms factories.

policies.name: Secret police
policies.description: Our political police and their informers will keep watch on our people.

policies.name: Border war
policies.description: Our troops will fight over a disputed border without either side declaring war.

policies.name: Extend direct rule
policies.description: Our head of state will appoint salaried governors and tax collectors to run our provinces directly.
policies.note: The counterpart of Consolidate the colonies, for ground a country holds in its own name but does not administer. Only a government that answers to nobody can post its own men over a district's own authority.

policies.name: Improve mining conditions
policies.description: We will limit miners' hours and set their wages and safety standards by law.
policies.note: The counterpart of Improve worker conditions, for the pits. Felt by what a province digs rather than by its factories, since the men a mine act reaches are not on a factory floor. The yield is named resource by resource because resourceYield is a map and there is no key for every dug kind at once.

policies.name: State of Alert
policies.description: We will keep our garrisons manned and our reserves at readiness the year round.
